messages:
Ava S: Hey team — customer reporting intermittent 502/504s on the web console. They say it happens when uploading a file. Asked for HAR + console logs so we can escalate. Can someone drop a short, cross-browser checklist (Mac + Windows + Safari) we can send to them?

SupportBot: Remember to include the request id (X-Request-Id or X-Req-Id) from the failing request, the exact local time (with timezone), and the user email (redact if required). :white_check_mark:

Mike R: Quick checklist we use (minimal, 5–7 steps):
1) Reproduce issue while recording: open browser devtools (Chrome/Edge: F12 or Cmd+Option+I, Safari: Develop -> Show Web Inspector).
2) In Network tab: check "Preserve log" and "Disable cache".
3) Clear existing logs, then reproduce the error (upload the file).
4) After reproduction, locate the failing request in Network, click, inspect Headers -> look for X-Request-Id/X-Req-Id (or our backend request-id header). Copy that value.
5) Right-click the network list -> "Save all as HAR with content" (Chrome/Edge). For Safari: Develop > Show Web Inspector > Network > right-click request list -> "Export HAR" (if not available, use Safari Technology Preview or use the HAR export extension).
6) Open Console tab, copy any red errors (console errors + stack traces).
7) Zip the HAR + console logs + a short repro note (steps, account id, local time, request id) and upload to https://support.redwood.com/upload (or attach to the ticket).

Sophie L: Sample curl to reproduce a simple upload-ish POST (replace <REDACTED_TOKEN> and <REQ_ID>):
```bash
curl -v -X POST "https://api.redwood.com/v1/console/upload" \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED_TOKEN>" \ 
  -H "X-Request-Id: <REQ_ID>" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: multipart/form-data" \ 
  -F "file=@/path/to/test-file" 
```
If they can run that from their terminal with the same file and token (or a short-lived token we provide), it often reproduces quickly.

Ava S: Nice. Add two small notes we always ask customers: (a) if they see an auth error include the full response headers & body, (b) if it's latency / timeout include the exact duration they observed.

DevEx: A couple of redaction tips before upload: replace any Authorization header values with <redacted>, remove cookies, and strip personal data from form fields. If the HAR includes sensitive POST bodies, ask the user to run a quick grep and redact: e.g., `jq 'del(.entries[].request.postData)' < input.har > sanitized.har`.

Mike R: Windows Edge steps (brief):
- F12 -> Network -> check "Preserve log" -> reproduce -> right-click -> Save as HAR with content.

Sophie L: If they can't produce HAR, ask for these fallback bits: network waterfall screenshot + full console transcript (copy all) + the failing request curl (right-click -> Copy -> Copy as cURL). That cURL is super helpful.

Ava S: Great — I'm going to paste this into the customer reply. Thanks all. :rocket:
